With a new "1-2-3" path to earn, members can start seeing value immediately and build toward even greater savings, OneKeyCash and travel perks as they progress through the program.
OneKeyCash remains flexible: every $1 in OneKeyCash is worth $1 toward eligible bookings across hotels, vacation homes, cars and activities—with no blackout dates.
How does free lounge access for delayed flights work for Expedia One Key members?
Expedia is enhancing its free lounge access benefit for delayed flights and extending eligibility to Gold members. Eligible members whose flight is delayed by 90 minutes or more can receive complimentary access to an airport lounge or other eligible airport experience. The benefit will initially operate as a pilot as Expedia continues to enhance the experience and evaluate member engagement. [1]
Eligible passes provide access to lounges in the LoungeKey network, including independent operators such as The Club, Escape Lounges, Plaza Premium, and Aspire. The benefit may also include participating airport bars and restaurants, spas, gaming lounges, and sleep pods. If no lounge or alternative option is available at the airport, each eligible passenger on the same itinerary receives $20 in OneKeyCash.
According to a recent consumer survey, almost half of U.S. travelers (48%) have experienced a flight delay of 90 minutes or more, while 54.1% find airport security stressful, including 12.3% who find it very stressful. Expedia customer feedback shows that providing eligible travelers with QR-enabled access to an in-terminal lounge can turn a frustrating disruption into a more comfortable experience.
What are the CLEAR Partnership benefits available to Expedia One Key members?
Through the CLEAR partnership, Expedia One Key members can access preferred pricing and services designed to make the airport experience more seamless. The CLEAR partnership gives U.S. One Key members access to tier-based discounts on CLEAR+ and CLEAR Concierge to help travelers have secure, stress-free experiences—from home to gate and back again.
Members can sign up for discounted CLEAR+ products through Expedia to move through security faster at more than 60 U.S. airports using secure identity verification. CLEAR Concierge provides a dedicated Ambassador to help guide travelers from the curb to their gate when they need an extra set of hands at the airport.
Through Expedia:
Platinum members: CLEAR+ annual Membership for $129. A Membership plus two CLEAR Concierge Departure Service bookings for $199.
Gold and Silver members: CLEAR+ annual Membership for $179. A Membership, plus two CLEAR Concierge Departure Service bookings for $249.
Blue members: CLEAR+ annual Membership for $209.
Silver, Gold and Platinum members: 20% off additional CLEAR Concierge Departure Service bookings.
Airport security is a meaningful source of stress, and travelers say they would use time saved at security for practical and enjoyable parts of the airport experience. According to the consumer survey: [2]
"Walk through security instantly" was selected by 23.2% as their preferred airport superpower, nearly as popular as automatic upgrades at 23.9%.
The time problem is tangible: The average typical security wait is 22.1 minutes. 44.3% usually wait at least 20 minutes, and 19.8% usually wait 30 minutes or more. Separately, 30.0% report that their longest-ever security wait was at least 60 minutes.
What is Expedia's One Key Price Drop Protection and how does it help me save money on flights?
Gold and Platinum members who book eligible flights in the Expedia app can receive free One Key Price Drop Protection. If the price drops before departure, Expedia automatically provides the difference in OneKeyCash.
After booking an eligible flight in the Expedia app and until the day the flight is scheduled to depart, Expedia automatically checks the price of the flight on Expedia once every 24 hours. Price checks are based on the flight details booked. Expedia will send notifications about any price changes. If the price of the eligible flight drops on Expedia, the traveler will get a Price Drop Protection Payment in OneKeyCash for the difference after the trip is completed.
In 2025, Expedia gave $28 million in OneKeyCash directly to Gold and Platinum One Key members through its Price Drop Protection program. [3]
How do members progress through One Key tiering status?
Members continue to advance through tiers by collecting trip elements as they travel—not simply by completing bookings. Members join as Blue, reach Silver after five trip elements, Gold after 15 and Platinum after 30. That means a new member can reach Silver after a single trip, such as two hotel nights and a three-day car rental. By recognizing the individual components of a journey, One Key gives members more ways to make progress toward higher status.
The program's tiered instant discounts remain available across a wide selection of hotels, car rentals and activities. The new earn structure replaces the previous flat 2% rate with a clearer, tiered approach:
Blue: 10% or more in instant discounts, plus 1% back in OneKeyCash
Silver: 15% or more in instant discounts, plus 2% back in OneKeyCash
Gold: 20% or more in instant discounts, plus 2% back in OneKeyCash
Platinum: 20% or more in instant discounts, plus 3% back in OneKeyCash
At the highest tier, Platinum members now earn One Key's highest standard rate—3% back in OneKeyCash—helping them build toward their next trip faster.
What rewards do One Key Credit Cardholders earn?
The One Key Credit Card delivers value on every trip and beyond, giving cardholders 3% back in OneKeyCash on Expedia bookings made with the card, including flights, plus an additional 3% for Silver Members, 4% for Gold Members and 6% for Platinum Members when booking VIP Access properties—up to 9% back on eligible VIP Expedia bookings.
Cardholders also earn 3% back on gas, groceries and dining, as well as 1.5% back everywhere else with the no-annual-fee card or 2% back with the Fee Card, making it easy to earn rewards on everyday purchases both within and beyond Expedia.
What else is changing for Expedia One Key members?
Expedia is simplifying or retiring selected lower-value and legacy features while investing in benefits designed to deliver more noticeable value.
Standalone flights no longer earn the previous 0.2% in OneKeyCash through the loyalty program.
Flights still count as an eligible trip element toward tier status.
Members can continue to use OneKeyCash on eligible flight bookings as before.
Package bookings earn OneKeyCash on the non-flight portions of the trip.
The Hotel Price Guarantee benefit is being sunset for new bookings.

A: Eligible U.S. One Key Gold and Platinum members and additional travelers on the same itinerary can receive complimentary access to an airport lounge or other eligible airport experience through Expedia, subject to the benefit terms.

A: Flights must be registered at least 24 hours before scheduled departure, and certain airlines are excluded.
Q: What happens if no lounge or alternative airport experience is available?
A: Each eligible passenger on the same itinerary receives $20 in OneKeyCash, subject to the benefit terms.

A. Eligible passes provide access to lounges in the LoungeKey network, including independent operators such as The Club, Escape Lounges, Plaza Premium, and Aspire. The benefit may also include participating airport bars and restaurants, spas, gaming lounges, and sleep pods; major airline-branded lounges are generally excluded.
Q: Why do travelers value lounge access during flight delays?
A: Among travelers who have experienced a flight delay, 83.0% consider a delay-related benefit valuable, and 30.5% prefer an airport lounge as a place to wait during a delay of 90 minutes or more.

A: CLEAR+ is an annual Membership that enables Members to move through security faster at more than 60 U.S. airports using secure identity verification.
Q: What is CLEAR Concierge?
A: CLEAR Concierge provides a dedicated Ambassador to help guide travelers from curb to gate.
Q: Who can access CLEAR benefits through Expedia?
A: U.S. One Key members can access CLEAR+ pricing and CLEAR Concierge options through Expedia based on their One Key status.

A: Expedia One Key is Expedia Group's free travel rewards program in the U.S., shared across Expedia, Hotels.com® and Vrbo®. Members receive Member Prices discounts, earn OneKeyCash on eligible bookings and share tier status across participating brands.

How Booking Holdings and Expedia Are Taking Opposite Bets on AI Shopping Agents
Meta's new shopping agent rattled online travel stocks almost equally, but Booking Holdings and Expedia chose opposite responses to the threat. One strategy leaves a company dangerously exposed if Meta decides to cut out the middleman entirely.
Published October 1, 2026, 9:05am ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A traveler uses a mobile app to plan their next trip, a common scenario for online travel agencies like Booking and Expedia. The rise of AI shopping agents presents new challenges and opportunities for these platforms. © CarmenMurillo / iStock via Getty Images
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META | META Price Prediction) launched Muse, a shopping agent that reached 560,000 daily active users within 11 days.
Truist then cut price targets on Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG) and Expedia Group (NASDAQ:EXPE) on the same day, citing Muse.
Both online travel agencies (OTAs) kept their ratings. Booking stayed at Buy with its target cut from $242 to $216, and Expedia stayed at Hold with its target cut from $309 to $288. The two companies responded to Muse differently, and Booking’s approach likely holds up better.
Expedia Joined Muse While Booking Kept Its Direct Channel
Expedia partnered with Muse and is integrated for travel booking there. That suits a company whose B2B revenue, which powers other brands’ travel sites, grew 23% last quarter.
Booking stayed out. Its consumer direct mix held in the mid-60% range for four quarters, and large language models send “significantly below one percent” of its room nights.
Partnering risks teaching Meta how travelers shop, which could help it bypass Expedia later, and declining risks missing agent-first travelers, a smaller cost while that traffic stays tiny.
Independent Hotels Keep Booking Essential to AI Agents
The same firm estimated that only about 10% of Booking’s room nights come from the top global hotel brands. Big chains run loyalty programs and booking systems an AI agent can plug into directly, but independent hotels lack that technology, so an agent seeking their rooms still needs Booking. Booking also processes payment on approximately 73% of gross bookings, which keeps it inside the transaction.
Both stocks have already absorbed similar damage.
Booking fell 17.98% over the past month, and Expedia fell 16.95%, nearly identical damage. Booking’s 25-to-1 stock split effective April 2, 2026 explains why its $162.91 shares look small beside Expedia’s $263.36. On forward earnings, Booking trades at 13 times and Expedia at 11 times.
Target Cuts Came With an Admission of Uncertainty
The firm warned that Meta poses “greater downside risks to OTAs given the company’s strong consumer position,” but admitted the “extent to which Muse or other AI agents will affect OTA bookings share remains highly uncertain.”
Retail shows the same split: Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) blocked Muse, while Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), Wayfair (NYSE:W) and Sephora joined as launch partners. Meta’s chief executive said Meta will profit from a small transaction fee, a toll that would likely come out of travel sellers’ margins.
Booking Looks Better Positioned to Withstand Muse
Booking looks better placed of the two. Revenue of $7.35 billion beat estimates, Transformation Program savings now target about $650 million by the end of 2027, and its hotel base sits further from Muse.
Expedia posted 14% revenue growth and raised guidance, but its partnership strategy leaves it more exposed if Meta’s fee pressures partner economics.
My view changes if Booking reports large language model traffic climbing well above 1% of room nights. Pair that with a direct mix sliding below the mid-60s, and Booking would be paying for customers it once owned.

Expedia Group Advertising and Redion Announce First Travel Protection Partnership
(Photo by scyther5/iStock/Getty Images Plus/Getty Images)
Expedia Group has signed its first travel insurance and assistance advertiser, bringing longtime protection provider Redion onto Expedia Group Advertising as a dedicated partner and opening a new advertiser category in the process.
Redion is the new global name for Europ Assistance, which operated in the U.S. as Generali Global Assistance. The company has supplied travel protection to Expedia Group customers for more than 15 years, but until now that relationship stopped at distribution. Under the September 22 agreement, the two will run co-branded editorial, on-platform placements, and targeted activations across Expedia Group brands, with the first efforts slated for the third quarter of 2026.
The deal fits a broader push by Expedia Group Advertising to sell reach beyond its core roster of hotels, airlines, and destination marketers. Over the past year the unit has run campaigns for retailers, entertainment companies, and financial services firms looking to get in front of travelers with a trip already in mind, both on Expedia Group’s own sites and apps and through offsite channels and partner publishers. Travel insurance straddles that line between travel and non-travel spend, which is the opening Redion intends to use.
Expedia Group’s own research suggests there is money on the table. The company found that 62% of travelers made a non-travel purchase connected to their most recent major leisure trip, spending roughly $500 on average beyond the trip itself, and that 38% of Gen Z travelers bought a financial product or service before departing.
“Opening a category is not something we do often,” said Jennifer Andre, vice president of business development at Expedia Group. “Redion earned this as our first insurance advertising partner because of a 15-year track record of protecting our travelers. Together we can bring travel protection into the journey earlier and more easily than either of us could alone.”
For Redion, the timing doubles as a brand launch.
“This partnership marks a defining moment for Redion,” said Virginie Babinet, CEO of travel insurance and assistance for Redion Group. “As we introduce the Redion brand to the world, we’re doing it from the center of the traveler’s journey, alongside a longstanding partner. We intend to make it a partnership that others are measured against.”

Mon, October 5, 2026 at 9:29 PM PDT 8 min read
Chicago, IL – October 6, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas features NVIDIA's NVDA, Alphabet's GOOGL, Meta Platforms META, Expedia EXPE, Apple AAPL and MongoDB MDB
According to NVIDIA's iconic CEO Jensen Huang, there are four waves of the artificial intelligence revolution:
1. Perception AI (2012): Started over a decade ago. Focused on core recognition tasks like speech recognition and image classification.
2. Generative AI: Dominated recent years and characterized by large language models like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Alphabet's Gemini that generate text, code, and images based on predictive patterns.
3. Agentic AI (Entering this Phase Now): Enables models to reason, plan, and perform complex multi-step tasks independently.
4. Physical AI (likely to be in 2027/2028): The next major industrial revolution. Integrates AI into real-world applications, advanced automation, and human-like robots that understand the laws of physics.
What is Agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that can act independently to achieve multi-step goals without human supervision. Investors can think of agentic AI applications as the technology equivalent of a personal assistant. Unlike traditional chatbots that only answer single prompts, agentic AI has agency. It breaks user's request into small steps, creates plans, uses tools (like external websites or APIs), and adapts to new information to complete an entire workflow on its own.
Imagine that you want to book the cheapest one-way flight from New York to London. Rather than manually searching through numerous websites, you can prompt an agentic AI application to do the work for you. Once the flight is found, the user merely has to confirm payment. Agentic AI can also be used in corporate settings. For instance, an e-commerce company can leverage agentic AI to conduct refunds. With clear rules, the AI system can decide whether a refund is allowed, process it automatically, update the in-house database, and create a shipping label. Agentic AI can even help financial companies to scan for fraud, automate loan approvals, and handle compliance checks.
Meta Launches "Muse" Personal AI Assistant
On September 8th, tech giant Meta Platforms launched "Muse," its first personal AI agent. Muse uses built-in intelligence to browse the internet and connect users to their favorite applications, like travel website Expedia or Google's Gmail.
Over the past few months, the number of AI product launches has been dizzying as tech companies look to cash in on the hype surrounding Wall Street's hottest industry, artificial intelligence. In September alone, OpenAI expanded the "GPT-6" universe, Anthropic released "Claude Opus 5.5," xAI launched "Grok 4.7," and Google updated its family of applications.
However, Meta's "Muse" launch is arguably the most significant application release thus far in the AI revolution. In fact, within just a handful of days, Muse jumped to #1 on the Apple App Store and Google Play. Meanwhile, according to Apptopia app analytics, Meta reached 1.1 million installs roughly 10 days after launch, surpassing ChatGPT's 2022 launch. For context, before the Muse launch, ChatGPT was the fastest-growing consumer application in history.
The business community widely recognizes Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg for his high-stakes, forward-looking business strategy. Zuck's business acumen perfectly embodies hockey legend Wayne Gretzky's famous philosophy:
"Skate to where the puck is going to be, not where it has been."
For instance, Zuckerberg understood the threat of mobile-first, photo-centric social media platforms. In 2012, he shelled out $1 billion for Instagram. At the time, critics scoffed at a $1 billion purchase for an app with fewer than 20 employees. Today, Instagram is worth between $250 and $350 billion.
Two years later, Zuckerberg saw that the future of global communication belonged to lightweight, cross-platform messaging networks. Zuckerberg paid a mind-boggling $19 billion for "WhatsApp," outbidding Google. Today, WhatsApp boasts 3.3 billion global monthly active users and is valued at well over $100 billion.
Despite the impressive track record, Zuckerberg and the Meta team still have their fair share of doubters. In fact, Meta shares have traded in a sloppy, frustrating price consolidation for two years.
However, investors are finally catching on to the potential of Meta's AI ambitions. In September, Meta shares jumped more than 25%, marking its largest monthly gain in over a decade.
In 2026, Meta spent more than $100 billion on its AI investments. In fact, Meta even poached top AI talent from industry peers for a cool $100 million. The enormous spending has created fear, uncertainty, and doubt across Wall Street. That said, Muse should dispel that fear. That fear has led to a reasonable 25x P/E ratio for Meta shares.
Wall Street Analysts Will Need to Play Catch-Up
Despite the fact that Meta just had the most successful AI launch in history, most Wall Street analysts have not raised their earnings revisions to reflect that success. Actually, more analysts tracked by Zacks Investment Research have lowered their targets for next quarter over the past 60 days.
Last week, MongoDB CEO CJ Desai jumped ship to run Meta's enterprise platform business, underscoring that Meta has a "rare advantage" across models, infrastructure and agents. Zuckerberg commented that:
"We believe superintelligence will create significant new opportunities for all people and businesses. Meta already serves billions of people at scale and helps hundreds of millions of businesses reach customers. Today we are starting the next major pillar of our business, Meta Enterprise Platform, to help businesses use AI to grow and transform in new ways as well. Meta Enterprise Platform will use our strengths that few other companies have: advanced models, leading agents, large-scale infrastructure, and years of working closely with many businesses. Initially, we will focus on bringing our full technology stack, including the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more to businesses and developers to help them grow."
Meta's move into the enterprise market is a brilliant one. Enterprise customers not only have deeper pockets, but they also tend to be stickier clients. According to The Business Research Company, the enterprise AI market will grow from ~$40 billion in 2026 to ~$164 billion by 2030, which assumes a juicy compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 42%.
If Meta shares can break out of the current multi-year base, the Fibonacci extensions suggest a target of $1,000 per share by the end of next year is reasonable.
As Meta bridges the gap between consumer-facing autonomy and high-value enterprise utility, the broader market is only beginning to wake up to what is happening. Backed by a robust technology stack, record-breaking adoption metrics, and massive long-term vision, Meta has positioned itself at the epicenter of the agentic revolution. For investors willing to look past near-term spending anxieties, the launch of Muse may well be remembered as the catalyst that sent Meta shares to $1,000.

Expedia Group to lay off 58 corporate employees
Expedia Group will lay off 58 employees at its Seattle headquarters, per a federal WARN notice. · Hotel Dive · Sean Gallup via Getty Images
This story was originally published on Hotel Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Hotel Dive newsletter.
Expedia Group will lay off dozens of corporate employees at its headquarters in Seattle, according to a letter sent to Washington state officials in accordance with the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act.
The permanent layoffs are expected to impact 58 employees holding a variety of titles at the company, per the WARN letter. They are expected to take effect between Nov. 21 and Dec. 1, 2026.
Expedia Group will lay off employees in data scientist, finance manager, senior accountant, senior financial analyst and software development engineer roles, among others. The company also plans to cut multiple vice presidents, per the letter.
Some of the layoffs "are the result of, or will result in, the relocation or contracting out of the employer's operations or the employees' positions," according to the letter.
Expedia Group declined to provide additional comment. The company owns Travelocity, Orbitz, Vrbo, Expedia, Hotels.com and other online travel booking platforms.
Across the travel sector, hospitality software provider Mews announced in July that it would lay off 15% of its staff in a pivot to an "AI-native" future.
Meanwhile, Marriott International confirmed earlier this month it is undergoing "organizational changes" as the result of a strategic review of its Customer Engagement Centers. The company laid off more than 800 corporate employees in 2024 as part of a companywide restructuring.

Expedia Makes Flying Easier with One Key Benefits: Lounge Access During Delays, Less Time at Airport Security and Money Back When Fares Drop
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:00 AM PDT 11 min read
SEATTLE, October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia® today introduced new Expedia One Key benefits designed to make travel easier from booking to boarding, giving travelers immediate value and savings, while helping them earn rewards for future trips. Expedia One Key is Expedia's free loyalty program, offering instant member discounts and OneKeyCash™ rewards that can be used on future eligible travel.
Expedia One Key's updated benefits include:
Free lounge access for delayed flights: Expedia is expanding free lounge access for delayed flights to eligible Gold and Platinum One Key™ members.
Discounted CLEAR+ membership and CLEAR Concierge services: Travelers can speed through airport security and get to their gate faster.
Price Drop Protection: If the price of an eligible booked flight drops before departure, Expedia automatically provides the fare difference in OneKeyCash™.
Instant Savings, while earning OneKeyCash: Expedia One Key members can enjoy instant discounts with Member Prices, plus earn 1% to 3% back in OneKeyCash to use on future travel.
"Travelers told us they want a loyalty program with rewards and perks program that delivers real savings right away while helping them earn rewards for future trips," said Casey Lehman, Vice President of Loyalty, Expedia Group. "We wanted to make our loyalty program simpler for our members, so we're strengthening our proposition of instant discounts plus rewards for future trips, while adding distinctive travel perks that support members from booking to boarding—including lounge access during delays, less time at airport security through our CLEAR partnership and OneKeyCash when a flight price drops."
What is new with Expedia One Key loyalty benefits?
Expedia One Key comes with two ways to save: instant discounts with Member Prices, plus OneKeyCash to use on future travel. With a new "1-2-3" path to earn, members can start seeing value immediately and build toward even greater savings, OneKeyCash and travel perks as they progress through the program.
OneKeyCash remains flexible: every $1 in OneKeyCash is worth $1 toward eligible bookings across hotels, vacation homes, cars and activities—with no blackout dates.
How does free lounge access for delayed flights work for Expedia One Key members?
Expedia is enhancing its free lounge access benefit for delayed flights and extending eligibility to Gold members. Eligible members whose flight is delayed by 90 minutes or more can receive complimentary access to an airport lounge or other eligible airport experience. The benefit will initially operate as a pilot as Expedia continues to enhance the experience and evaluate member engagement. [1]
Eligible passes provide access to lounges in the LoungeKey network, including independent operators such as The Club, Escape Lounges, Plaza Premium, and Aspire. The benefit may also include participating airport bars and restaurants, spas, gaming lounges, and sleep pods. If no lounge or alternative option is available at the airport, each eligible passenger on the same itinerary receives $20 in OneKeyCash.
According to a recent consumer survey, almost half of U.S. travelers (48%) have experienced a flight delay of 90 minutes or more, while 54.1% find airport security stressful, including 12.3% who find it very stressful. Expedia customer feedback shows that providing eligible travelers with QR-enabled access to an in-terminal lounge can turn a frustrating disruption into a more comfortable experience.
What are the CLEAR Partnership benefits available to Expedia One Key members?
Through the CLEAR partnership, Expedia One Key members can access preferred pricing and services designed to make the airport experience more seamless. The CLEAR partnership gives U.S. One Key members access to tier-based discounts on CLEAR+ and CLEAR Concierge to help travelers have secure, stress-free experiences—from home to gate and back again.
Members can sign up for discounted CLEAR+ products through Expedia to move through security faster at more than 60 U.S. airports using secure identity verification. CLEAR Concierge provides a dedicated Ambassador to help guide travelers from the curb to their gate when they need an extra set of hands at the airport.
Through Expedia:
Platinum members: CLEAR+ annual Membership for $129. A Membership plus two CLEAR Concierge Departure Service bookings for $199.
Gold and Silver members: CLEAR+ annual Membership for $179. A Membership, plus two CLEAR Concierge Departure Service bookings for $249.
Blue members: CLEAR+ annual Membership for $209.
Silver, Gold and Platinum members: 20% off additional CLEAR Concierge Departure Service bookings.
Airport security is a meaningful source of stress, and travelers say they would use time saved at security for practical and enjoyable parts of the airport experience. According to the consumer survey: [2]
"Walk through security instantly" was selected by 23.2% as their preferred airport superpower, nearly as popular as automatic upgrades at 23.9%.

What is Expedia's One Key Price Drop Protection and how does it help me save money on flights?
Gold and Platinum members who book eligible flights in the Expedia app can receive free One Key Price Drop Protection. If the price drops before departure, Expedia automatically provides the difference in OneKeyCash.
After booking an eligible flight in the Expedia app and until the day the flight is scheduled to depart, Expedia automatically checks the price of the flight on Expedia once every 24 hours. Price checks are based on the flight details booked. Expedia will send notifications about any price changes. If the price of the eligible flight drops on Expedia, the traveler will get a Price Drop Protection Payment in OneKeyCash for the difference after the trip is completed.
In 2025, Expedia gave $28 million in OneKeyCash directly to Gold and Platinum One Key members through its Price Drop Protection program. [3]
How do members progress through One Key tiering status?
Members continue to advance through tiers by collecting trip elements as they travel—not simply by completing bookings. Members join as Blue, reach Silver after five trip elements, Gold after 15 and Platinum after 30. That means a new member can reach Silver after a single trip, such as two hotel nights and a three-day car rental. By recognizing the individual components of a journey, One Key gives members more ways to make progress toward higher status.
The program's tiered instant discounts remain available across a wide selection of hotels, car rentals and activities. The new earn structure replaces the previous flat 2% rate with a clearer, tiered approach:
Blue: 10% or more in instant discounts, plus 1% back in OneKeyCash
Silver: 15% or more in instant discounts, plus 2% back in OneKeyCash
Gold: 20% or more in instant discounts, plus 2% back in OneKeyCash
Platinum: 20% or more in instant discounts, plus 3% back in OneKeyCash
At the highest tier, Platinum members now earn One Key's highest standard rate—3% back in OneKeyCash—helping them build toward their next trip faster.
What rewards do One Key Credit Cardholders earn?
The One Key Credit Card delivers value on every trip and beyond, giving cardholders 3% back in OneKeyCash on Expedia bookings made with the card, including flights, plus an additional 3% for Silver Members, 4% for Gold Members and 6% for Platinum Members when booking VIP Access properties—up to 9% back on eligible VIP Expedia bookings.

Expedia is simplifying or retiring selected lower-value and legacy features while investing in benefits designed to deliver more noticeable value.
Standalone flights no longer earn the previous 0.2% in OneKeyCash through the loyalty program.
Flights still count as an eligible trip element toward tier status.
Members can continue to use OneKeyCash on eligible flight bookings as before.
Package bookings earn OneKeyCash on the non-flight portions of the trip.
The Hotel Price Guarantee benefit is being sunset for new bookings.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META | META Price Prediction) launched Muse, a shopping agent that reached 560,000 daily active users within 11 days.
Truist then cut price targets on Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG) and Expedia Group (NASDAQ:EXPE) on the same day, citing Muse.
Both online travel agencies (OTAs) kept their ratings. Booking stayed at Buy with its target cut from $242 to $216, and Expedia stayed at Hold with its target cut from $309 to $288. The two companies responded to Muse differently, and Booking’s approach likely holds up better.
Expedia Joined Muse While Booking Kept Its Direct Channel
Expedia partnered with Muse and is integrated for travel booking there. That suits a company whose B2B revenue, which powers other brands’ travel sites, grew 23% last quarter.
Booking stayed out. Its consumer direct mix held in the mid-60% range for four quarters, and large language models send “significantly below one percent” of its room nights.
Partnering risks teaching Meta how travelers shop, which could help it bypass Expedia later, and declining risks missing agent-first travelers, a smaller cost while that traffic stays tiny.
Independent Hotels Keep Booking Essential to AI Agents
The same firm estimated that only about 10% of Booking’s room nights come from the top global hotel brands. Big chains run loyalty programs and booking systems an AI agent can plug into directly, but independent hotels lack that technology, so an agent seeking their rooms still needs Booking. Booking also processes payment on approximately 73% of gross bookings, which keeps it inside the transaction.
Both stocks have already absorbed similar damage.
Booking fell 17.98% over the past month, and Expedia fell 16.95%, nearly identical damage. Booking’s 25-to-1 stock split effective April 2, 2026 explains why its $162.91 shares look small beside Expedia’s $263.36. On forward earnings, Booking trades at 13 times and Expedia at 11 times.
Target Cuts Came With an Admission of Uncertainty
The firm warned that Meta poses “greater downside risks to OTAs given the company’s strong consumer position,” but admitted the “extent to which Muse or other AI agents will affect OTA bookings share remains highly uncertain.”
Retail shows the same split: Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) blocked Muse, while Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), Wayfair (NYSE:W) and Sephora joined as launch partners. Meta’s chief executive said Meta will profit from a small transaction fee, a toll that would likely come out of travel sellers’ margins.
Booking Looks Better Positioned to Withstand Muse
Booking looks better placed of the two. Revenue of $7.35 billion beat estimates, Transformation Program savings now target about $650 million by the end of 2027, and its hotel base sits further from Muse.
Expedia posted 14% revenue growth and raised guidance, but its partnership strategy leaves it more exposed if Meta’s fee pressures partner economics.
My view changes if Booking reports large language model traffic climbing well above 1% of room nights. Pair that with a direct mix sliding below the mid-60s, and Booking would be paying for customers it once owned.

According to NVIDIA's iconic CEO Jensen Huang, there are four waves of the artificial intelligence revolution:
1. Perception AI (2012): Started over a decade ago. Focused on core recognition tasks like speech recognition and image classification.
2. Generative AI: Dominated recent years and characterized by large language models like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Alphabet's Gemini that generate text, code, and images based on predictive patterns.
3. Agentic AI (Entering this Phase Now): Enables models to reason, plan, and perform complex multi-step tasks independently.
4. Physical AI (likely to be in 2027/2028): The next major industrial revolution. Integrates AI into real-world applications, advanced automation, and human-like robots that understand the laws of physics.
What is Agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that can act independently to achieve multi-step goals without human supervision. Investors can think of agentic AI applications as the technology equivalent of a personal assistant. Unlike traditional chatbots that only answer single prompts, agentic AI has agency. It breaks user's request into small steps, creates plans, uses tools (like external websites or APIs), and adapts to new information to complete an entire workflow on its own.
Imagine that you want to book the cheapest one-way flight from New York to London. Rather than manually searching through numerous websites, you can prompt an agentic AI application to do the work for you. Once the flight is found, the user merely has to confirm payment. Agentic AI can also be used in corporate settings. For instance, an e-commerce company can leverage agentic AI to conduct refunds. With clear rules, the AI system can decide whether a refund is allowed, process it automatically, update the in-house database, and create a shipping label. Agentic AI can even help financial companies to scan for fraud, automate loan approvals, and handle compliance checks.
Meta Launches "Muse" Personal AI Assistant
On September 8th, tech giant Meta Platforms launched "Muse," its first personal AI agent. Muse uses built-in intelligence to browse the internet and connect users to their favorite applications, like travel website Expedia or Google's Gmail.
Over the past few months, the number of AI product launches has been dizzying as tech companies look to cash in on the hype surrounding Wall Street's hottest industry, artificial intelligence. In September alone, OpenAI expanded the "GPT-6" universe, Anthropic released "Claude Opus 5.5," xAI launched "Grok 4.7," and Google updated its family of applications.
However, Meta's "Muse" launch is arguably the most significant application release thus far in the AI revolution. In fact, within just a handful of days, Muse jumped to #1 on the Apple App Store and Google Play. Meanwhile, according to Apptopia app analytics, Meta reached 1.1 million installs roughly 10 days after launch, surpassing ChatGPT's 2022 launch. For context, before the Muse launch, ChatGPT was the fastest-growing consumer application in history.
The business community widely recognizes Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg for his high-stakes, forward-looking business strategy. Zuck's business acumen perfectly embodies hockey legend Wayne Gretzky's famous philosophy:
"Skate to where the puck is going to be, not where it has been."
For instance, Zuckerberg understood the threat of mobile-first, photo-centric social media platforms. In 2012, he shelled out $1 billion for Instagram. At the time, critics scoffed at a $1 billion purchase for an app with fewer than 20 employees. Today, Instagram is worth between $250 and $350 billion.
Two years later, Zuckerberg saw that the future of global communication belonged to lightweight, cross-platform messaging networks. Zuckerberg paid a mind-boggling $19 billion for "WhatsApp," outbidding Google. Today, WhatsApp boasts 3.3 billion global monthly active users and is valued at well over $100 billion.
Despite the impressive track record, Zuckerberg and the Meta team still have their fair share of doubters. In fact, Meta shares have traded in a sloppy, frustrating price consolidation for two years.

The enormous spending has created fear, uncertainty, and doubt across Wall Street. That said, Muse should dispel that fear. That fear has led to a reasonable 25x P/E ratio for Meta shares.

Despite the fact that Meta just had the most successful AI launch in history, most Wall Street analysts have not raised their earnings revisions to reflect that success. Actually, more analysts tracked by Zacks Investment Research have lowered their targets for next quarter over the past 60 days.

Backed by a robust technology stack, record-breaking adoption metrics, and massive long-term vision, Meta has positioned itself at the epicenter of the agentic revolution.
